I am 38 years old, finished primary school, and came back to farming three years ago after working outside. I have 16.1 mu of land in Quzhou, five mouths to feed at home, and a well for water. I am not one of those old farmers with forty years of experience, but I have been watching my neighbors carefully and copying what works.

My land is split like this: 7.5 mu I keep for wheat in winter and maize in summer — that is the double-crop system everyone around here does. The other 8.6 mu I use for vegetables. Eggplant is my main money crop, so I put 5 mu there. I do 2 mu of cabbage in spring and 1.6 mu of cauliflower in autumn. I learned this layout from the farmer two rows over. He has been doing it for years and makes decent money.

For wheat, I use improved seed I buy from the shop — not the fanciest kind, but it gives about 500 kg per mu if I do things right. Last year I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as basal, and then I topdressed with urea twice. This year I will do the same: total about 26 kg of nitrogen per mu, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium. I irrigate three times — winter water from the well, then jointing water, then one more before heading. I spray insecticide three times and herbicide once. I rotary-till before sowing.

For maize, I plant hybrid seed — Denghai or something similar — right after the wheat comes out in June. Everyone uses hybrid now; the yield is just better, around 550 kg per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the holes at planting and then urea at the big喇叭口 stage. Total nitrogen about 22 kg per mu, phosphorus 6 kg, potassium 5 kg. I irrigate twice in summer if the rain is not enough. I spray for insects two or three times, herbicide once, and sometimes a plant regulator. I do not till much for maize — there is no time after wheat harvest, so it is basically no-tillage.

Eggplant is where I spend the most money, but it is also where I earn the most. I buy hybrid seedlings from the dealer — 5 mu needs a lot of seedlings. I put down plenty of compost and compound fertilizer before transplanting, and then I topdress every couple of weeks. Eggplant loves potassium, so I make sure to give it enough. Total I use about 35 kg nitrogen per mu, 12 kg phosphorus, and 25 kg potassium. I water every seven to ten days in the hot months, so about ten times total. I have to spray a lot — whiteflies and mildew are terrible — about twenty times counting insecticide, fungicide, and regulators. I rotary-till deep in spring. If I do everything right I should get 4,000 kg per mu.

Cabbage is on 2 mu in spring. I buy hybrid seed. It needs less than eggplant but still eats plenty. I give it 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 8 kg phosphorus, 10 kg potassium. Water five times, spray six times. Rotary tillage. Yield should be around 4,000 kg per mu.

Cauliflower is on 1.6 mu in autumn. Similar to cabbage but I give it a bit less nitrogen — 15 kg per mu, 7 kg phosphorus, 10 kg potassium. Four irrigations, five sprays. Rotary tillage. I expect about 3,000 kg per mu.

I worry about costs. Fertilizer went up in price. But I would rather put a little too much than too little. A bad harvest means I lose everything; wasting some fertilizer is just money I spent. I watch what my neighbors do. If Old Wang puts two bags of urea on his maize, I do the same. With 16 mu I hire three or four people for eggplant transplanting and harvest season — my family cannot do it all. That is extra cost, but eggplant pays for it.
